clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman with negative family history of cancer presented in February 2019 with 2 months of intermittent hematochezia. Laboratory evaluation showed mild anemia (Hb 108 g/L). Abdominal CT imaging revealed thickening and eccentricity of the intestinal wall in the lower rectum-anal canal with local lumen constriction and enlarged surrounding lymph nodes. Surgical resection was performed, and histopathology confirmed anorectal malignant melanoma with immunohistochemical staining positive for HMB-45, Melan-A, S100, and Vimentin, and negative for PCK and P16. Twenty-nine months later (approximately November 2021), during a CT scan performed for staging purposes, a newly visible 2.3 cm nodule with unclear boundaries was identified in the outer upper quadrant of the right breast, considered a neoplastic lesion. Core needle biopsy under ultrasound guidance confirmed malignant tumor. Modified radical mastectomy was subsequently performed. Histopathology of the breast specimen confirmed metastatic malignant melanoma with immunohistochemical staining positive for HMB-45, Melan-A, S100, and Vimentin, and negative for CK, CK7, CD34, and WT-1, establishing the breast lesion as a metastasis from the anorectal primary melanoma.

Twenty-nine months after anorectal surgery, CT scan identified 2.3 cm nodule in right breast outer upper quadrant with unclear boundaries
Core needle biopsy of right breast under ultrasound guidance revealed malignant tumor
Modified radical mastectomy was performed with histologic confirmation of metastatic malignant melanoma
